title: Persephone — Ritual and worship
summary: Persephone, queen of the underworld, divides her year between Hades and her mother Demeter. This study follows the myth into temples and festivals.
body:
Persephone, queen of the underworld, divides her year between Hades and her mother Demeter. Her story explains the cycle of the seasons.

Myths were not entertainment; they were scripts for ritual. Persephone was enacted in festivals, sacrifices, and mysteries that bound communities together and aligned human time with cosmic time. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Persephone is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

Where the myth was performed, it was believed with the body, not just the mind. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Osiris and Loki.
